sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Generic boilerplate ('Stress in Agta usually falls on the penultimate syllable.. Stress is phonemic in Agta', with a Tagalog-looking example báta/batá); cites no author, year or fieldwork. Not a source.

sources.citation: UP Diliman Department of Linguistics, The Katig Collective. 2024. Language capsule 'Agta, Katubung'. https://linguistics.upd.edu.ph/the-katig-collective/language-capsules/agta-katubung/
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; bibliographic page. Cites Imperial 2018 as '[Unpublished thesis]. University of the Philippines Diliman' and says it covers 'sound inventory, word formation processes, and basic clause structures'; reports 12 speakers in 2018.

sources.citation: Lobel, Jason William. 2013. Philippine and North Bornean languages: Issues in description, subgrouping, and reconstruction. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa. Sec. 3.2.3 'The Agta of Camarines Sur, Bikol: Rinconada Agta, Partido Agta, and East Lake Buhi Agta', pp. 67-70; sec. 8.2.9 'Contrastive Accent', p. 259.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing for Inagta Partido/Isarog Agta: sec. 3.2.3 is a sociolinguistic and subgrouping note with pronoun, case-marker and demonstrative tables (Partido forms carry accent marks, e.g. akó, iká, iyá, didiyán, dodoón, but no rule is stated). The only accent statement (8.2.9, p. 259: 'accent.. is contrastive in Manide and Inagta Alabat') concerns two other languages.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page for isar1235 (references and alternative names).
sources.note: Lists no descriptive reference: only Reid 1994 (subclassification, p.c. Lobel 2012), Campbell et al. 2022 (endangerment), Lewis 2009. Confirms no grammar/phonology entry in Glottolog.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Says 'Stress is typically penultimate but may shift for contrast', but the page itself states its phonology is 'inferred from comparative studies' and 'Due to sparse data'; cited only to Lobel 2013, which contains no such statement. Not a source; recorded so it is not mistaken for one.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No phonology section and no stress statement; its value is the reference to Imperial 2018 (BA thesis, May 2018, UP Diliman) and Lobel 2013 pp. 68-69.

sources.citation: Zorc, R. David, Jason W. Lobel & William Hall. (submitted, n.d.). The History of the Philippine Languages. Chapter draft, zorc.net.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only subgrouping: 'Inagta, a language spoken by the Agta of Mt. Isarog and Mt. Iriga' placed inside the Bikol subgroup (sec. 2.7.1.3); footnote 2 treats Mt. Iraya Agta as not distinct from Inagta Mt. Isarog and Mt. Iriga. Accent discussed only at the Proto-Philippine level, no statement for Isarog Agta.

sources.citation: Imperial, Irvin Jen P. 2018. Katubungi: A grammatical description of Isarog Agta (Katubung) and some notes on language endangerment and extinction. BA thesis, Department of Linguistics, University of the Philippines Diliman (May 2018). Unpublished.

sources.note: The only grammatical description of the language ever. its abstract says it covers the 'inventory of sounds', so a stress statement (if any exists) will be here. Fieldwork at Brgy. Pinit, Ocampo, Camarines Sur.
